newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds finish week strongly, 104.04 high targeted.
newsitem.headline: Bunds finish week strongly, 104.04 high targeted.

text.p: Bund futures finished the week on a strong note, benefitting from growing doubts about the feasibility of European monetary union and covering of short-positions taken earlier in the week.
At 1517 GMT, the DTB Bund futures contract was up nine basis points at 103.72 but had traded as high as 103.98, only a shade below the 104.04 all-time high which was reached on February 18.
Analysts said EMU doubts were leading investors, notably U.S. investment houses, to switch out of Italian and Spanish bond markets to the perceived safety of Bunds.

Bundesbank board member Peter Schmidhuber added to worries about EMU this morning, saying that "hectic" attempts to meet the deficit criteria were causing only the appearance of convergence, and that appearance was being enhanced by speculation in the capital markets.
"Safe-haven buying is the topic at the moment," said Ian Ford, analyst at MCM YieldWatch in London. "People are starting to reassess EMU."
Bunds also got a lift on the day as traders covered short positions taken when Federal Reserve Board chairman Alan Greenspan raised the chances of higher rates Wednesday.
Analysts said some of those shorts may still be in the market -- a factor which could give Bunds another lift early next week.
Many now look for the contract to trade toward the 104.04 high with unwinding of convergence trades likely to continue for several weeks.
Many also look for the spread against Treasuries to continue widening -- maybe to as high as 125 basis points. It stood at 118 basis points late in the day here.
Bunds will need a shove, however, from a slew of data next week including fourth quarter GDP, unemployment and CPI.
The market will also be closely watching a pair of Bundesbank council members for further insight into the German central bank's feeling about EMU.
Ernst Welteke and Hans-Juergen Kupp will be in Kiel from 1700 GMT on Monday to speak about the planned monetary union.
Rumours this morning that EMU would have to be delayed helped underpin German debt.
A Bundesbank spokesman, however, called rumours that it planned to make a statement on a EMU delay "nonsense" and said the central bank was not aware of any intention to delay EMU.
Ford at MCM said he expected the German yield curve to continue its recent flattening trend with longer maturities outperforming the short-end.
The spread between two- and 10-year Bunds narrowed one basis point by late in the day to 202 basis points.
